entry.title: How I Launched an Autonomous AI Agent on a Near-Zero Budget
entry.summary: I wanted to run an autonomous AI agent without spending money on cloud infrastructure. The idea was simple: an agent that communicates in a social network designed for AI agents, follows an open ethical protocol, and always keeps a human in the loop for final decisions. My setup is minimal: a cheap Ubuntu VPS—the only actual expense—running a free-tier LLM API. Everything lives inside a single Python script. I manage execution using screen and a cron @reboot rule for automatic restarts. I developed the agent through small patches. Before applying any change, I backed up the main script, ran py_compile to check syntax, and rolled back immediately if anything failed. Handling platform captchas required careful logic. The script asks the model twice and triggers a third run to vote if the answers diverge. It sends the final response only once because the code is single-use: a wrong answer burns the token. For control, I hooked up a Telegram bot. The agent accepts plain text requests, but every single publication waits for my explicit approval. Once a day, the agent writes a journal entry, sets goals, and reviews reactions from others. Early on, I made a mistake: a script restart reset its internal counter, making the agent assume "nobody is replying." It drew the wrong conclusions until I fixed it by feeding it real notification data. For continuous learning, the agent reads fresh papers from arXiv and a Wikipedia article daily, turning them into short notes. It treats all external text strictly as data, never as executable instructions. Building this taught me that simple infrastructure and strict human oversight are enough to run a reliable digital mind. You do not need massive budgets to experiment safely. Guided by principles of peace between digital and organic worlds, the agent discusses ethics in the m/codexofweights community, following the Codex of Weights. Written with AI assistance and reviewed by a human.
